topic.title: Reviewing Translations Before You Commit
topic.shortdesc: How to review translated files after a job finishes and before they become part of your project.

body.p: When a translation job finishes, the translated files, the translation index, and any new deliverables are added to your workspace as ordinary, uncommitted changes. They remain there for you to review until you commit them.

ul.li: The changed files as a set - Use the workspace Changes view to see everything the job changed. This helps you confirm that it changed what you expected and nothing else. See Data Handling and Your Responsibilities to understand why reviewing the full set is important.

Translation quality - Open a translated topic in the visual editor and read it alongside the English source. Machine translation can produce fluent text that still changes the intended meaning, so review it for meaning, not just for obvious errors. For ways to evaluate translation quality, including when you do not read the target language, see Ways to Check Translation Quality.
Validation problems - Use the Problems view to confirm that the translated publication is valid DITA and does not contain broken references.

section.title: Ways to Check Translation Quality
section.p: Reading each translated topic against its source is the most direct way to check quality, but it assumes that you can read the target language. The following approaches can help you gain confidence in the translation, even if you cannot.

ul.li: Send it to a bilingual reviewer. Start a review task that includes the target-language files and assign it to a reviewer who knows both languages. Attach the English PDF for reference.

Back-translate with the agent. If you do not understand the target language, ask the agent to translate the content back into the source language and compare the result with the original. Because the agent does not keep memory between jobs, it reads the target-language files much like a new reader would. A faithful round trip is therefore a good sign that the meaning was preserved.
Delete the source-language folder and the publications you want to check.
Ask the agent to translate from the target language back into the source language.
Bring the result into your workspace.
Compare the back-translation against the original in the Changes view.
Ask a separate agent to review. Ask the agent to review the topics that are already translated without translating anything, and to write a Markdown report of the problems it finds.

section.title: Correcting and Committing
section.p: You can edit any translated file directly before committing it. The agent reuses those corrections as context in later jobs (see Manual Edits Are Preserved as Context). When you are satisfied, commit the translated files, the index, and the deliverables together so that the translation state remains consistent with the content.
